title: Electric field of a point charge

step.script: A positive point charge creates an electric field directed radially outward. These arrows show the force direction on a positive test charge.

ops.content: Electric field of a point charge

step.script: Field strength means force per unit positive test charge. For a point source, its magnitude follows an inverse-square law.

ops.content: r: distance from the source charge

step.script: Doubling the distance spreads the same source's influence: the field becomes one quarter as strong, not one half.

checkpoint.question: If the distance triples, what fraction of the original field remains?
checkpoint.expected_gist: One ninth, because field strength is inversely proportional to distance squared.

step.script: Magnitude depends on charge size and distance. Direction points outward for positive sources and inward for negative sources; a negative test charge feels opposite force.

ops.content: Positive source: outward. Negative source: inward.
